items.Sentence: The treatment system at JWPCP consists of screening, grit removal, primary sedimentation...
Wastewater effluent from the bar screens is directed to one of six grit chambers, which remove heavy inorganic material.
Wastewater from the grit chambers is then directed to the sedimentation tanks for settleable and floatable solids removal.

Effluent from the primary sedimentation tanks is biologically treated in pure oxygen activated sludge reactors...each stage with three aerators/mixers...The first stage of the reactors is operated as an anaerobic selector...the fourth stage...functions as a pH adjustments stage.
After passing through the biological reactors, wastewater flows into the final clarifiers to separate the activated sludge solids...
A dissolved air flotation thickening system is used to concentrate the waste activated sludge produced in secondary treatment.
Ultimately the skimmings are directed to one of 24 circular anaerobic digesters...Anaerobic digestion of the sludge reduces the concentration of pathogens...
The pumps are used to deliver digested sludge to the centrifuges, which are used to separate water from the suspended solids...Diluted cationic polymer is used in the process to enhance flocculation.
Eighteen storage silos, each of which can hold up to 510 tons, store the biosolids prior to conveyance to truck loading stations.
Secondary effluent is disinfected using a bleach solution to achieve a chlorine residual of approximately 1-2 mg/L...

Methane gas generated in the anaerobic digestion process is used to produce power and digester heating steam in a total energy facility that utilizes gas turbines and waste-heat recovery steam generators.
During periods when the gas turbines are not operational, digester gas can be burned at two different flare stations...
Three compressors are used to compress the digester gas...to approximately 350 pounds per square inch (psig).
Centrate from the centrifuges is collected and gravity flows to the Centrate Treatment System Facility, where solids are concentrated using dissolved air flotation.
There is one pumping station per reactor...that pumps activated sludge to the inlet of the reactors to keep an effective concentration of microorganisms in the reactors.
